source: ~/dev/brain/docs/RUNBOOK-two-accounts.md — the runbook is canonical; this is its checklist form. Edit both together.

sections.title: Log in, then govern it before anything else
sections.warning: DO NOT RUN ANYTHING ON THE RESERVE BETWEEN STEPS 1 AND 2. Claude Code reads its hooks, settings and CLAUDE.md from the config directory. A freshly logged-in account has an identity and no ruleset: no ship gate, no US-English check, no claim-check, no blanket-staging refusal. It is not neutral, it is ungoverned.

items.note: Then /login as the reserve (4lot.org) account. Run nothing else in it.
Mirror the guardrails. This must be the very next thing after the login.
Prove it, do not assume it: each hook must be registered in settings.json AND present on disk. A file without a registration guards nothing; a registration without a file fails silently.

sections.title: Park every session first
sections.warning: A live session's context IS its transcript, and the transcript belongs to the account that made it. No environment variable moves it. Step 1 is the entire mitigation: it turns a lost conversation into a document both accounts can read. Skipping step 1 is the only way to actually lose work here.

items.note: Every session writes a handoff into brain.

items.text: Switch the account in the client, or export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR

items.note: The new sessions read the handoffs.
